ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a metered RydeTAXI service, so the fare varies with distance and any unexcused extra kilometres are refundable [F6][RD-0][RD-2]. The GPS record shows one off-route segment, 17:41–17:44, covering 1.76 km where the optimal route covers 0.03 km, i.e. 1.73 extra km [F3][RD-1].

No exemption applies. The driver's accident excuse appears only in his post-trip statement [F10]; it is a statement, not a traffic record, and the trace settles RD-4 as failed for this segment because the only incident (17:16 on Seletar Expressway, 0 m from the optimal route) does not qualify under the trace's RD-4(a) screen and a speed band alone does not exempt [F10][F13][F11][RD-4]. On RD-5 I read the whole chat: it contains only the rider's pickup message and the driver's arrival message, both at 17:24, well before the segment start, and neither names any road, area or route — the rider's "main entrance in a blue shirt" is a pickup arrangement, not agreement to a detour [F7][F8][F9]. The driver's claim of consent lives only in his statement, which is a claim and not consent [F10][RD-5]. The chat record is complete and timestamped and holds no rider agreement, so the finding is counts, not undetermined [F9][RD-5]. RD-3 also does not apply: nothing in the record shows the rider named a stop or that any stop was made on this segment [F7][F8][RD-3].

Amount: distance fare $27.23 ÷ 19.3 km = $1.4102/km [F6]; 1.73 extra km × $1.4102 = $2.4397 → $2.44, refund under RD-2 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The 0.37 km difference between the billed 2.1 km excess and this segment's 1.73 km is map-matching residual (≤ 0.25 km) and is not refundable, and the fixed platform/base/time components are unaffected [F4][F6][RD-2].

No account flag: the trace settles RD-6 as failing, since the profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so this is not a "repeated" breach [F16][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint — no threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or dangerous-driving allegations; the complaint is a fare/routing dispute [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

The segment's 1.73 extra km is therefore unexcused under RD-1 and refundable under RD-2 [F3].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your fare dispute and are refunding $2.44 to you as a Ryde voucher.

The GPS trace showed one off-route stretch on your metered taxi trip: 1.73 km beyond the direct route between 17:41 and 17:44. Metered fares move with distance, so those extra kilometres are refundable. The rest of the fare — base, platform and time charges — stands. The small gap between the total distance billed and this one segment isn't refundable.

The amount is paid as a Ryde voucher on your account. No action is needed from you. The driver's record has been noted.

DRIVER: We reviewed a routing dispute on your metered taxi trip and are refunding $2.44 to the rider as a Ryde voucher.

The GPS trace showed one off-route segment between 17:41 and 17:44 covering 1.73 km more than the optimal route. Your post-trip statement about an accident, and your claim that the rider agreed to the route, were both considered. The trip chat contains only the pickup and arrival messages, sent at 17:24, and neither agrees to any detour, so the extra distance is refundable under the route rules.

This is recorded as a breach on your record. No account flag applies, as you have no prior upheld route disputes in the last 90 days.

notices.text:
We reviewed your fare dispute and are refunding $2.44 to you as a Ryde voucher.

The GPS trace showed one off-route stretch on your metered taxi trip: 1.73 km beyond the direct route between 17:41 and 17:44. Metered fares move with distance, so those extra kilometres are refundable. The rest of the fare — base, platform and time charges — stands. The small gap between the total distance billed and this one segment isn't refundable.

The amount is paid as a Ryde voucher on your account. No action is needed from you. The driver's record has been noted.

We reviewed a routing dispute on your metered taxi trip and are refunding $2.44 to the rider as a Ryde voucher.

The GPS trace showed one off-route segment between 17:41 and 17:44 covering 1.73 km more than the optimal route. Your post-trip statement about an accident, and your claim that the rider agreed to the route, were both considered. The trip chat contains only the pickup and arrival messages, sent at 17:24, and neither agrees to any detour, so the extra distance is refundable under the route rules.

This is recorded as a breach on your record. No account flag applies, as you have no prior upheld route disputes in the last 90 days.
